introduction.heading: Plumbing for Wasatch County homes
introduction.body:
Half of the homes in Wasatch County were built in 2005 or later, and about 18% before 1980, according to the U.S. Census Bureau. In newer homes like these, the first big plumbing jobs are often water heaters, fixtures and water softeners as the original equipment ages. A water heater usually lasts 10 to 15 years.

Each town in Wasatch County has its own water system. Heber City uses groundwater from Broadhead Spring and three wells, and the Jordanelle Special Service District serves the Jordanelle Basin, including water from the Ontario Drain Tunnel.

Jordanelle Reservoir, just north of Heber, holds up to 363,000 acre-feet behind a 296-foot dam on the Provo River, mainly for city and industrial water supply.
